detail.abstract: Sudan's ongoing conflict cannot be adequately analyzed through the lens of internal political dysfunction alone. This paper introduces the Geopolitical Conflict Matrix (GCM)-a structured analytical framework adapted from systems biology's microenvironmental modeling-to map the competing resource extraction strategies of seven external actors operating within Sudanese territory. We identify five strategic resource categories: Red Sea/Port Sudan access, gold, agricultural land, Blue Nile hydraulic position, and oil pipeline infrastructure, and score each actor's stake intensity across these dimensions on a 0-5 ordinal scale. Our analysis reveals that Sudan functions as a "contested host state"-a territory in which multiple sovereign and non-sovereign actors simultaneously extract resources while the host government's capacity deteriorates. Key findings: (1) the UAE-RSF-Wagner triangle constitutes a selffinancing gold-military closed-loop system independent of the formal state; (2) Egypt faces a structural contradiction between needing Sudan weak and needing it stable; (3) Ethiopia's GERD strategy provides hydraulic leverage over both Egypt and Sudan simultaneously; (4) captured political parties are the primary internal mechanism transmitting external interests into Sudanese governance. We propose four structural interventions targeting resource decoupling as prerequisites for conflict resolution.

title: Geopolitical Risks in the Post-Cold War Era : 'Make America Great Again' can be 'Make the World Great Again'

detail.title: Geopolitical Risks in the Post-Cold War Era : 'Make America Great Again' can be 'Make the World Great Again'
detail.abstract: This study explores the post-cold war era by investigating geopolitical risks from the Middle East to the Korean Peninsula. Geopolitics is a fleeting reality and is a matter of a few top decision makers while ordinary people catch a glimpse of it by the press. Due to the relative inaccessibility of key information, geopolitics is hard to study even if it is a crucial element to shape our era. To fill the gap, we adopt a copula approach to surmise a joint probability distribution between the geopolitical risk in the world and several countries. This method could capture tail dependence. The highest upper tail dependence with the world's geopolitical risk has been that of Israel; as one moves from the cold war to the post-cold war period, the increasing cases of upper tail dependence are China, Korea, Russia, and Ukraine while decreasing cases are Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey. It implies that the world's flashpoints might have been shifting from the Middle East to Asia as our eras have been gone through the cold war and the post-cold war periods. Seemingly self-centered 'Make America Great Again' could be 'Make the World Great Again'. The best is yet to come.

title: Quantifying the Economic Impact of Risk: The R-index Approach

detail.title: Quantifying the Economic Impact of Risk: The R-index Approach
detail.abstract:
This study introduces the R-index as a novel framework for quantifying the economic impact of risk through realized deviations from expected performance. In contrast to traditional risk measures that rely on probabilistic or volatility-based approaches, the proposed index captures risk as an outcome-based phenomenon directly linked to firm-level performance. The R-index is constructed as a normalized measure of deviation between actual and expected values and is further extended to a multidimensional setting, allowing for aggregation across different performance indicators. The empirical analysis is conducted using longitudinal financial data from three firms operating in distinct sectors of the Montenegrin economytelecommunications, retail, and tourism-over the period 2015-2024. 

The results reveal substantial heterogeneity in the realization of risk across firms, even under identical macroeconomic conditions. While some firms exhibit stable performance and limited deviations, others demonstrate pronounced volatility and sensitivity to external shocks, particularly during the COVID-19 period. These findings suggest that risk is not uniformly transmitted but is instead shaped by firm-specific characteristics, including operational structure and adaptive capacity. 

The study contributes to the literature by redefining risk as a realized economic phenomenon and by proposing a scalable and interpretable metric that bridges risk measurement and performance evaluation. The R-index offers practical relevance for managerial decisionmaking and provides a foundation for future research on the relationship between risk and firm value.

title: Who Sent This Agent? Cryptographic Organizational Identity for the Autonomous Agent Economy

detail.title: Who Sent This Agent? Cryptographic Organizational Identity for the Autonomous Agent Economy
detail.abstract: The emerging autonomous agent economy requires a payment capability that no existing rail provides: microtransactions with accountability. Fiat payment rails provide accountability but cannot support micro-transactions — minimum fees of ~$0.30 make sub-dollar payments uneconomical, and human authorization requirements are incompatible with autonomous operation. The Lightning Network provides micro-transactions but not accountability — payments are anonymous by default, and API providers cannot determine which organization authorized a payment. Without provable accountability, vendors will not accept cryptocurrency payments regardless of the technical advantages. We propose a hierarchical identity system using BIP-32 key derivation that enables cryptographic proof of organizational membership without requiring private key disclosure. Our design uses hardened derivation for sensitive organizational levels (organization, team, project) and non-hardened derivation for ephemeral levels (agent, instance), with the non-hardened levels extending to arbitrary depth for multi-agent orchestration, enabling providers to verify agent membership using only public keys. Combined with Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) for budget-constrained payments, this architecture provides non-custodial, verifiable identity for the emerging agent economy. We analyze security properties, compare with existing solutions, and discuss deployment considerations.

title: Northern Corridor—Arctic Maritime Transport Integration for Central Asia

detail.title: Northern Corridor—Arctic Maritime Transport Integration for Central Asia
detail.abstract:
Russian rivers famously ‘go the wrong way.’ The United States and Canada have the supremely beneficial hydrography of the interconnected Great Lakes system and the Mississippi, and Europe has the Rhine, Elbe, Danube, and Dnieper inland waterways giving even landlocked states such as Switzerland and Austria direct access to the ocean and the favourable cost-savings that maritime transport brings to trade. But for Kazakhstan, one Russia river does ‘go the right way.’ The Ob’Irtysh river system penetrates deep into the heart of Eurasia from the Arctic Ocean.


The development on Kazakhstan’s inland waterways though is extremely undeveloped. Kazakhstan has over 4,000 kms of navigable inland waterways, comparable with the Western European industrialised economies of Germany and France. Kazakhstan could never rival a state like the Netherlands for interconnected networked inland waterways, but the natural geography presented is similar to Switzerland on the Rhine or Austria on the Danube: land-locked developed economies with access to the global ocean.

China’s Belt and Road in the CAREC economies has come with media hype on the benefits of the shorter transit times offered by the China Rail Express intercontinental rail corridors connecting China and Europe via either Russia or the Black Sea. The policy argument is that there is sufficient demand for goods with transport time-needs shorter than maritime but cheaper than air freight.

title: SARS: A Novel Face and Body Shape and Appearance Aware 3D Reconstruction System extends Morphable Models
affiliations: University of Hull, University of Sheffield - INSIGNEO Institute for in silico Medicine, University of Hull and University of Hull

detail.title: SARS: A Novel Face and Body Shape and Appearance Aware 3D Reconstruction System extends Morphable Models
detail.abstract: Morphable Models (3DMMs) are a type of morphable model that takes 2D images as inputs and recreates the structure and physical appearance of 3D objects, especially human faces and bodies. 3DMM combines identity and expression blendshapes with a basic face mesh to create a detailed 3D model. The variability in the 3D Morphable models can be controlled by tuning diverse parameters. They are high-level image descriptors, such as shape, texture, illumination, and camera parameters. Previous research in 3D human re-construction concentrated solely on global face structure or geometry, ignoring face semantic features such as age, gender, and facial landmarks characterizing facial boundaries, curves,dips, and wrinkles. In order to accommodate changes in these high-level facial characteristics, this work introduces a shape and appearance-aware 3D reconstruction system (named SARS by us), a c modular pipeline that extracts body and face informationfrom a single image to properly rebuild the 3D model of the human full body. SARS improves accurate semantic surface editing to capture expression-driven facial muscle deformationand appearance changes for different genders, while maintaining identity. SARS has three transformation modules. In our experiments, the system showed promising results on the 3DHumans dataset and other publicly available datasets.

title: Curbing Short-Termism: Patient Capital and Managerial Myopia
affiliations: Southwest University, Southwest University, University College London and Chongqing University - School of Economics and Business Admininstration

detail.title: Curbing Short-Termism: Patient Capital and Managerial Myopia
detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of the deepening reforms in China's capital market, fostering and expanding patient capital has become a key strategic initiative for promoting high-quality economic development and supporting the development of new quality productive forces. Examining its governance effects therefore carries important theoretical value. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2024, this study empirically investigates the impact of patient capital on managerial myopia. The results show that patient capital significantly inhibits managerial short-termism. This finding remains robust after a series of endogeneity and robustness tests, including the instrumental variable approach, system GMM estimation, and alternative measures of the core variables. Mechanism analyses indicate that patient capital exerts its governance effect through two channels: improving internal control quality and increasing ownership concentration. The former strengthens the institutional foundation for decision-making oversight, while the latter enhances the long-term monitoring incentives of large shareholders; together, these channels curb managerial short-term behavior. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that the governance effect of patient capital is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, firms receiving high analyst attention, and firms in the growth stage, suggesting that its effectiveness depends on the coordinated support of both internal and external governance environments.

title: Exchange Prediction with High Frequency Data in an Emerging Market: The Experience of Costa Rica Between 2012 And 2025
affiliations: Universidad de Costa Rica

detail.title: Exchange Prediction with High Frequency Data in an Emerging Market: The Experience of Costa Rica Between 2012 And 2025
detail.abstract: This paper establishes a cointegration relationship for the nominal exchange rate in Costa Rica. The reporting requirements for the central bank allow me to calculate a daily measure of its dollar shortfall from trading with nonbank public companies. This and the the country's differential Emerging Market Bond Index (EMBI) are cointegrated with Costa Rica's exchange rate. Out-of-sample tests show that forecasts based on these cointegration relationships significantly outperform a random walk benchmark. I also show that informed traders with data that is only a few days more recent can generate significantly better forecasts than those available to regular investors.

title: Advanced Medical Image Security Using Chaotic LSTM-Generated Keys and GAN-Based Encryption
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Advanced Medical Image Security Using Chaotic LSTM-Generated Keys and GAN-Based Encryption
detail.abstract: The secure transfer and storage of medical images continue to be a problem mainly because of the patient's private information. This study introduces a new framework for medical image encryption and decryption that combines deep learning and chaotic systems. The technique applies Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for the generation of dynamic keys, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for encryption and decryption of images, and a logistic map-based chaotic system to increase the level of encryption complexity. After the decryption process, the Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN) is utilized to enhance the quality of the images. The LSTM model takes the input image and produces a very large dynamic key which is then given to the GAN generator to start the encryption of the image. Next, the security is made even stronger with a logistic map-based chaotic transformation. For decryption, the inverse chaotic function and a synchronized GAN generator recover the original image using the same dynamic key. Security and experimental results show that the proposed scheme offers a large key space, high key sensitivity, low pixel correlation, strong resistance to statistical and differential attacks, and high visual fidelity of decrypted images. These results indicate that the framework is effective and robust for secure medical image transmission and storage.

title: CAYAS: A Tractable Framework for Portfolio Allocation with Dated Commitments

detail.title: CAYAS: A Tractable Framework for Portfolio Allocation with Dated Commitments
detail.abstract: Individual investors must finance binding commitments (a property purchase, education, retirement) through an uncertain market environment while holding assets they cannot trade freely. Classical portfolio theory treats the liquid portfolio in isolation and cannot adjust risk to the proximity of these commitments. We propose a numerically tractable Asset-Liability Management framework that reframes portfolio choice as a dynamic balance-sheet problem, treating liquid assets, illiquid assets, liabilities, and future cash flows jointly. The framework combines three components: (i) robust calibration of liquid-asset moments through Black-Litterman, (ii) a total efficient frontier that incorporates illiquid exposures and future commitments as balance-sheet constraints, and (iii) Bellman backward induction that yields a dynamic policy adjusting risk-taking endogenously to the proximity and severity of financing needs. Simulations provide two validation facts. In liability-free settings, the dynamic policy recovers the optimal Merton rule, confirming that the additional complexity introduces no artificial distortion. When financing constraints become binding, it generates a precautionary pattern: it reduces liquid-sleeve risk ahead of constrained expenditures and rebuilds exposure once the commitment is met, with an adjustment intensity that scales with the liability-to-wealth ratio.

title: Phase Transitions and Spatial Complexity: Modeling Land-use in Southeast France
affiliations: Université Côte d'Azur, Université Côte d'Azur, Université Côte d'Azur, Université Côte d'Azur and Université Côte d'Azur

detail.title: Phase Transitions and Spatial Complexity: Modeling Land-use in Southeast France

declarations.funderStatement: IDEX Académie d'Excellence 3 of Université Côte d'Azur.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates how introducing explicit spatial features alters phase-transition dynamics in economic land-use models. Building upon a recent hybrid agent-based and equation-based model of agricultural land-use transitions (Lopez-Merino et al., 2024), we incorporate real-world geographical constraints-rivers, valleys, and irreversible urbanization-observed in a case study of the Alpes-Maritimes region in Southeast France. Our simulations reveal that adding an urban land-use state and coastal development bias dampens the potential for agricultural resurgence after collapse. However, natural features such as valley corridors counteract this effect by fostering new agricultural clusters, even spurring greater agricultural recovery than in the non-spatial base model. Moreover, spatial dependencies in urban development (e.g. cities expanding near existing urban centres and along rivers) create secondary feedbacks that shape land-use outcomes in ways a non-spatial model would miss. These findings highlight the complex interplay between economic dynamics and spatial constraints: the latter can fundamentally change equilibrium outcomes and transition pathways. By integrating spatial complexity into a phase-transition framework, the study bridges equilibrium-based economic models and complexity-driven spatial approaches. The results yield new insights into regional resilience and sustainable land-use planning, suggesting that policies fostering agricultural revival must account for territories heterogeneities and the irreversibility of urban growth.

title: Source apportionment and health risk prioritization of groundwater contamination in a coal-mining area: An integrated SOM-PMF-Monte Carlo framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, China Medical University and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - State Key Laboratory of Urban and Regional Ecology

detail.title: Source apportionment and health risk prioritization of groundwater contamination in a coal-mining area: An integrated SOM-PMF-Monte Carlo framework
detail.abstract: In arid/semi-arid coal-mining regions, groundwater quality is increasingly threatened by intensive anthropogenic disturbances. However, quantitatively linking specific pollution sources to probabilistic health outcomes—and further translating this understanding into risk-based management priorities—remains a critical challenge. This study addresses this gap by developing an integrated framework combining self-organizing maps (SOM), positive matrix factorization (PMF), and Monte Carlo simulation to systematically decipher groundwater contamination sources and prioritize associated health risks, using the Huolingol mining area in Inner Mongolia, China, as a representative case. SOM analysis recognized three hydrochemical clusters: Cluster 1 (Na-HCO3/Ca-Na-HCO3 type), influenced by cation exchange and silicate weathering under alkaline conditions, exhibited elevated F- and NH3-N concentrations. Cluster 2 (Ca-Na-SO4/Ca-Na-HCO3 type) was characterized by elevated TDS, TH, SO42-, and NO3-, indicating significant anthropogenic impact. Cluster 3 (Ca-HCO3 type) represented the natural background with minimal contamination. Source apportionment using PMF revealed that human-driven composite pollution is the main cause of water quality evolution, with the mixed source of coal mine drainage and industrial/domestic wastewater contributing the highest proportion (22.42%), highlighting the overwhelming impact of mining and industrial activities. Monte Carlo simulation demonstrated that children face 33.9% probability of exceeding the safe threshold (HI>1)—1.75 times the adult risk level (19.4%), with F- and SO42- as primary risk drivers. By quantitatively linking specific pollution sources to probabilistic health outcomes, this study provides a transferable framework for identifying priority pollutants and vulnerable populations in complex contamination settings, offering actionable insights for groundwater management in water-stressed mining regions worldwide.

title: Adapted Belly Dance for Breast Cancer Survivorship and Post-treatment Recovery

detail.title: Adapted Belly Dance for Breast Cancer Survivorship and Post-treatment Recovery

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human participants were recruited and no original patient-level or participant-level data were collected for this manuscript. The paper is based on previously published literature only; therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No Funding

detail.abstract: Breast cancer survivorship frequently involves a prolonged period of physical, emotional, and social readjustment. Even after primary treatment has ended, many women report fatigue, body-image disruption, upper-limb symptoms, movement apprehension, reduced self-confidence, and difficulty maintaining regular physical activity. Exercise and supportive movement-based programs are therefore central to contemporary survivorship care, yet many women do not adhere to generic exercise prescriptions over time. Adapted belly dance may offer a valuable complementary option because it is low-impact, rhythmically engaging, culturally meaningful for many participants, and naturally integrates postural control, trunk mobility, upper-limb expression, and psychosocial re-engagement. This educational paper synthesizes existing literature on dance-based interventions in breast cancer survivorship, including belly-dance-specific studies and related supportive-care evidence, and translates that literature into a structured, practice-oriented framework for instructors and community programs. The paper does not claim that belly dance replaces medical rehabilitation, oncology care, lymphoedema management, or individualized exercise prescription. Rather, it positions adapted belly dance as a potentially useful supportive modality when screening, dosage, progression, and referral boundaries are handled responsibly. The paper proposes a staged instructional model, outlines contraindication-aware screening priorities, identifies common movement adaptations for posttreatment participants, and discusses how carefully delivered belly dance may contribute to quality of life, body image, self-esteem, social connection, movement confidence, and selected upper-limb and functional outcomes. A detailed implementation model is provided for non-clinical and rehabilitationadjacent settings. The goal is to offer an academically grounded but practically usable resource that can support community programming, educational dissemination, and future scholarly discussion on culturally tailored movement in survivorship care.

title: Large Language Models and Stock Investing: Is the Human Factor Required?
affiliations: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) and Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV)

detail.title: Large Language Models and Stock Investing: Is the Human Factor Required?
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can generate reliable stock market predictions. We evaluate four state-of-the-art models -ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Perplexity- across three prompting strategies: a naïve query, a structured approach, and chain-of-thought reasoning. Our results show that LLM-generated recommendations are hindered by recurring reasoning failures, including financial misconceptions, carryover errors, and reliance on outdated or hallucinated information. When appropriately guided and supervised, LLMs demonstrate the capacity to outperform the market, but realizing LLMs' full potential requires substantial human oversight. We also find that grounding stock recommendations in official regulatory filings increases their forecasting accuracy. Overall, our findings underscore the need for robust safeguards and validation when deploying LLMs in financial markets.

title: Importance of Weekly and Monthly Call and Put Option Jumps for Establishing Short-Term Predictions in the North American Equity Market
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Importance of Weekly and Monthly Call and Put Option Jumps for Establishing Short-Term Predictions in the North American Equity Market
detail.abstract:
This research article proposes a break from the traditional distinction between technical and quantitative analysis, introducing the KC2 model as a methodological bridge. The study critiques the limitations of classic indicators such as the Put-Call Ratio and proposes, instead, the use of options as precise sensors of market microstructure. The research is based on a sample of 16 large-cap stocks from the U.S. market, analyzed using high-frequency data at 5-minute intervals extracted from TradingView during two critical periods: a period of normal volatility (December-January) and a period of high volatility (February-March). The core of the work lies in decomposing asset movements into three cumulative variables: the market component (intraday), the gap component (overnight), and the total market.

The methodology demonstrates that the visual intersection of these components on cumulative scatter plots allows for the automatic identification of market tops and bottoms, revealing the exact moment of peak institutional hedging and, consequently, the detection of price peaks and troughs in the spot asset. The study initially uses At-the-Money (ATM) options to detect inflection points under normal volatility regimes, but the model adapts to systemic risk and “black swan” scenarios such as the conflict following the U.S.-Iran attacks by analyzing different levels of moneyness. It is validated that, during periods of high implied volatility, the flow of information shifts toward Out-of-the-Money (OTM) and In-the-Money (ITM) strikes, which act as indicators of panic and capitulation.

In addition, the article introduces “dynamic” or realized delta, a cumulative metric that allows the Greek letters to be integrated directly into graphical analysis. Unlike static delta, this tool reveals turning points by reflecting the actual behavior of market makers as they neutralize their positions. In conclusion, the study establishes a framework that overcomes “retail blindness,” demonstrating that most local lows are formed by the interaction between the underlying asset and put options, due to the mandatory hedging patterns of market makers in response to detected risk.

title: Two-Asset Digital Barrier Options via Wedge Heat Kernels: A Parabolic Extension of the López-Sinusiá Exit Problem
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Two-Asset Digital Barrier Options via Wedge Heat Kernels: A Parabolic Extension of the López-Sinusiá Exit Problem
detail.abstract: <div><p>This paper makes four contributions to the analysis of two-asset digital barrier options via wedge heat kernels. First, the stationary drift-diffusion exit problem on a wedge [14] is extended to the finite-horizon parabolic setting. A one-parameter family of contracts indexed by κ ∈ [0, r] is introduced: κ = r prices deferred payment (holder receives $1 at expiry if the paying barrier is hit first), κ = 0 prices immediate payment (holder receives $1 at the hitting time), and intermediate κ interpolates between the two. Symmetry and a no-arbitrage identity reduce pricing to a single basis problem V (κ) B . Second, a boundary-driven reformulation (Rκ) is derived: after a decorrelating coordinate change and drift removal, the remaining non-trivial time dependence of V (κ) B</p><p>is shown to be carried entirely by the paying sector boundary. In the general wedge, the resulting Duhamel representation does not collapse to a single Sommerfeld-type contour integral. Third, for uncorrelated assets (ρ = 0), the two-dimensional Poisson kernel factorises exactly, yielding a unified single-integral formula valid for all κ ∈ [0, r]. The integrand is the product of a first-passage density (Asset 1 to its barrier) and a survival probability (Asset 2 above its barrier), weighted by e -(r-κ)σ : deferred payment (κ = r) corresponds to the bare first-passage probability; immediate payment (κ = 0) to its Laplace transform at rate r. Fourth, the framework is extended to asset-or-nothing digitals via a change of numeraire: a single Girsanov drift shift yields a finite-horizon closed-form formula (A B ) of the same single-integral structure, together with its perpetual limit, thereby extending the framework in two directions not previously treated in closed finite-horizon form.</p></div>

title: The Daughter Effect in Politics: Evidence from Japanese National Legislators
affiliations: Waseda University, , Waseda University and Waseda University

detail.title: The Daughter Effect in Politics: Evidence from Japanese National Legislators
detail.abstract: We examine how politicians' family structure shapes policy preferences, focusing on the influence of daughters on attitudes toward gender-and family-related policies. Using original data on the number and gender of children of candidates elected to Japan's House of Representatives in 2021, combined with candidate survey responses collected during the election campaign, we analyze whether exposure to daughters affects positions on optional separate surnames for married couples, same-sex marriage, and legislation promoting understanding of sexual minorities. Exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in the number of daughters conditional on the number of children, we find that daughters are associated with more progressive policy positions among male candidates. Our findings highlight the role of family-based socialization in shaping elite political preferences and extend evidence on the "daughter effect" to a non-Western context.

title: Getting Ahead of Mistakes: Targeting Public Outreach with Machine Learning
affiliations: U.S. Department of the Treasury,  and U.S. Department of the Treasury

detail.title: Getting Ahead of Mistakes: Targeting Public Outreach with Machine Learning
detail.abstract: Public agencies must allocate preventive outreach before costly mistakes occur. We develop an anticipatory targeting framework that ranks households by baseline mistake risk Y (0)-rather than by heterogeneous treatment effects-and translates predictions into an implementable policy by choosing the outreach threshold to equate the model's statistical tradeoffs (false positives vs. false negatives) with an economically calibrated welfare tradeoff. We apply the approach to persistent non-claiming of the American Opportunity Tax Credit using linked IRS-SSA data. Even with moderate predictive accuracy (AUC ≈ 0.70), welfare calibration yields a stable rule that targets roughly half of households while capturing nearly the welfare gains of universal outreach at substantially lower fiscal cost. The results demonstrate how embedding machine learning within an explicit economic objective function transforms predictive risk scores into disciplined, welfare-improving policy rules.

title: Collective Narcissism in American Politics: A Historical Reflection

detail.title: Collective Narcissism in American Politics: A Historical Reflection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research received no external funding. No institutional affiliation.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that collective narcissism — defined here as the organization of group identity around a shared villain, sustained through the need for external validation and the destruction of perceived opponents — is not a contemporary pathology in American politics but its foundational operating system. Tracing the arc from the Revolutionary period through Reconstruction, the industrial era, and into the present, the paper demonstrates that the same psychological architecture has been continuously reproduced across different moral languages and institutional contexts. The founding exceptionalism that made revolution possible became the template for westward expansion, then fractured irrecoverably at the Civil War into two competing virtue claims — each requiring the other to sustain its own identity. In the modern period, this architecture was operationalized explicitly by the political right through religious and nationalist framing, then adopted invisibly by the political left through humanitarian causes whose institutional capture produced a closed validation loop insulated from accountability. Drawing on the Canon's framework of institutional convergence without coordination, the paper argues that contemporary media and digital infrastructure did not create this operating system but discovered it as the most profitable product ever encountered — stabilizing, rewarding, and scaling division in ways that benefit a class of infrastructure owners with no political home and no accountability to any electorate. The paper introduces the concept of the Exhausted Middle — citizens without a narcissistic organizing myth and therefore without political power — and situates collective narcissism as the psychological mechanism underlying the Canon's broader findings on narrative centralization and institutional drift.

title: Support for Democracy: Attitudinal versus Revealed-Preference Measures
affiliations: Yale University and Yale University - Department of Political Science

detail.title: Support for Democracy: Attitudinal versus Revealed-Preference Measures
detail.abstract: How well do our most frequently employed survey indicators of support for democracy measure that concept? We contrast such conventional, attitudinal measures and revealed-preference measures. The latter are based on voting for candidates in experimentally manipulated scenarios that mimic real-world electoral trade-offs between democratic principles and competing political considerations. We find that all attitudinal measures overstate the depth and breadth of support for democracy around the world. Two popular measures exhibit either no or a reverse relationship to experimentally revealed commitment to democracy, resulting in potentially misleading findings. This is because conventional measures fail to gauge whether attitudinally expressed support for democracy is deep enough to translate into costly pro-democratic actions. Nonetheless, a subset of attitudinal measures performs well on three baseline criteria that we develop to assess their performance: monotonicity, coverage, and discriminating power. These findings are robust to a range of alternative explanations and statistical techniques and hold across a large number of countries with diverse levels and histories of democracy. We propose a number of recommendations for how to improve the measurement of support for democracy.

title: The Squeeze Kernel Covariance Estimator: Dual-Timescale Tracking with Adaptive Shrinkage

detail.title: The Squeeze Kernel Covariance Estimator: Dual-Timescale Tracking with Adaptive Shrinkage
detail.abstract: We introduce the Squeeze Kernel covariance estimator, a streaming, PSD-by-construction method that combines three complementary components: (i) a dual-timescale EWMA separating fast volatility from slow correlation dynamics, (ii) a smooth kernel weight w t = d2 t /(d2 t + κ), motivated by the Fisher information of the Gaussian likelihood, that filters uninformative calm-day observations, and (iii) an adaptive equicorrelation shrinkage rule α t = max(0, n/(2S t)-δ) that automatically calibrates regularisation to the concentration ratio using the estimator's own effective sample size-requiring no cross-validation or tuning. We show that the complete update is a natural gradient ascent step on the Gaussian log-likelihood surface, with the kernel weight acting as an adaptive learning rate. On 53 global futures (1995-2026), the Squeeze Kernel matches DCC on out-of-sample negative loglikelihood while exhibiting far superior parameter robustness (10.5 vs. > 15,000 NLL range across a 50× parameter sweep). On S&P 500 equities, the adaptive shrinkage enables scaling to n=200 and n=500 stocks, beating DCC (-1,545 vs.-1,511) and all competing methods at high dimensions. In volatility-targeted portfolio applications with realistic institutional constraints, the Squeeze Kernel and DCC deliver comparable risk control-both achieving 35% lower volatility-tracking error than shrinkage baselines on 200 equities-while maintaining stable correlation dynamics through the COVID-19 crash. Formal Diebold-Mariano tests, VaR backtesting, and Monte Carlo simulations with Gaussian and Student-t innovations support all claims.

detail.abstract: Integrating smallholder farmers into high-value agricultural chains has emerged as a critical strategy to improve farm incomes in developing countries. Integration offers opportunities for smallholder farmers to advance beyond production, potentially engaging in higher-value activities such as product design, marketing, and distribution. This study examines the impact of strategic partnerships on the resources and sustainability of smallholder deciduous fruit growing enterprises within these high-value chains. Using hierarchical linear regression analysis, the research evaluates how these partnerships influence the resource base and long-term viability of these enterprises. The findings reveal that while strategic partnerships facilitate the production of high-quality fruit, thus boosting the supply base and competitiveness of exporting firms, there are limitations. Specifically, the study indicates that investments from strategic partners serve primarily to improve the quality of production rather than to build autonomous marketing capabilities among smallholder farmers. Moreover, the degree of commitment of smallholder farmers to these partnerships, coupled with the nature of resource investments, is significantly correlated with an adverse effect on the farmers' overall sustainability. Farmers should thus explore alternative marketing opportunities outside the confines of these strategic partnerships to foster entrepreneurial growth and ensure the sustainability of their farming enterprises. The findings have significant implications for the livelihood strategies of smallholder deciduous fruit farmers, particularly in terms of balancing the benefits of partnership with long-term sustainability goals.

detail.title: Survival Analysis and Continuous Covariates for Annuitant Data: A Mixture Modelling Approach
detail.abstract: A mixture modelling framework is proposed for the analysis of base mortality rates in pension scheme data, including continuous covariates such as benefit amount. Discretizing such a covariate loses information and may create spurious anomalies in financial values across values of the covariate. The mixture model combines a parametric time-to-event hazard and a simple probabilistic model for the continuous covariate, and the resulting hazard function: (a) varies  smoothly with the value of the continuous covariate; and (b) allows for non-proportional and potentially non-monotonic effects. Additionally, the mixture approach may identify latent groups of scheme members sharing a similar mortality profile. Inference of the model parameters is fully Bayesian, and is illustrated using a UK pension dataset for which there is evidence for heterogeneous mortality patterns driven by benefit amount. The mixture model with a regularized structure of the component-specific parameters outperforms simpler regression models and mixtures with fixed number of components. Additional analyses suggest that the approach provides a flexible and interpretable tool for modelling mortality differentials associated with continuous covariates, suitable for actuarial use.

title: Normative Solution and Real Solution: A Unified Theory of Market Deviation

detail.title: Normative Solution and Real Solution: A Unified Theory of Market Deviation
detail.abstract:
Traditional economics is built upon basic assumptions such as complete information and rational agents, and these assumptions together have given rise to a vast and coherent economic system. Yet it has long been criticized for being detached from reality and for depicting an ideal world that does not actually exist. Although behavioral economics, incomplete-information theory, and research on irrational decision-making have provided formulations that are closer to reality, these revisions have often remained local in scope and have failed to form a unified analytical framework.
This paper proposes a new perspective: we need not choose between the ``ideal'' and the ``real,'' nor must we reject the theoretical value of traditional economics as a whole. Rather, we may regard the world described by traditional economics as a normative ideal world. Accordingly, the demand corresponding to its basic assumptions is defined as normative demand X, while the real economic world---one that includes advertising, information asymmetry, behavioral biases, hidden charges, and related factors---is treated as the actual economic world, and the systematically rewritten unified demand within it is defined as real demand A[X]. By embedding both into a market-equilibrium framework, we can construct a framework for representing the real economy.
This approach not only allows us to handle various revisions in a unified way, but also enables us, within the same market-equilibrium framework, to use the two as separate inputs and derive two comparable sets of results: the normative solution and the real solution. In this way, once cost differences are introduced, firms' behavior, profits, and conditions of viability can be compared across the two cases.
The core findings of this paper can be summarized at three levels. First, the reason the real solution can persist over the long run is not that it better satisfies efficiency in the normative sense, but that it continues to dominate in the ranking of real profits. When the sum of the additional gains firms obtain from demand distortion and the equivalent gains from concealed cost reduction exceeds the cost of maintaining that distortion, market competition will not eliminate ``cheaters''; on the contrary, it will systematically allocate resources to the firms most capable of distorting demand. Second, this mechanism also reveals an inherent tension in the role of the entrepreneur: under the same logic of profit maximization, the entrepreneur appears as a creator of value under normative demand, but may emerge as an exploiter of consumer demand bias under real demand. The entrepreneur's dual social image thus receives a natural explanation. Third, the effect of external governance is not linearly cumulative, but threshold-based. Only when governance becomes strong enough to alter firms' profit structure, so that the expected profit advantage of the real solution over the normative solution turns from positive to negative, will the market switch from the distorted equilibrium back to the normative equilibrium.
More fundamentally, these findings pose a basic challenge to the core economic idea of the ``invisible hand'': the market mechanism itself has no intrinsic value orientation; it rewards only those behaviors that generate profit. Whether the invisible hand promotes efficiency or amplifies distortion depends on the structure of profit sources. When profits primarily reward genuine productive capability, it directs resources toward the normative solution; when profits primarily reward the ability to distort demand, it directs resources toward the real solution. This framework provides a unified analytical language for understanding misleading practices, hidden charges, and algorithmic manipulation in the platform economy.

title: A Transparent, Data-Driven Framework for Warranty Premium Estimation
affiliations: KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB), KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB) and Ghent University

detail.title: A Transparent, Data-Driven Framework for Warranty Premium Estimation
detail.abstract: Despite the widespread use of product warranties, setting their price remains a difficult task: They must ensure financial robustness by covering the expected warranty costs, but they must also offer transparency so that the pricing team can meaningfully incorporate these estimates into product price setting. However, many existing approaches still depend on ad hoc models that lack transparency. This paper presents a data-driven framework for estimating warranty costs, which involves predicting warranty claim frequency and claim severity separately using heterogeneous product-customer characteristics. We introduce a surrogate modeling approach to balance predictive accuracy with interpretability: an ensemble model identifies non-linear patterns and interactions, which are then translated into segmented features for a generalized linear model. This produces transparent, coefficient-based justifications while retaining most of the ensemble's predictive performance. Using data from a Tier 1 automotive supplier, we show how our method substantially improves on statistical benchmarks for both return rates and costs, while enabling traceable, feature-level justifications. Based on the predictive distributions, we derive risk-loaded warranty prices using Valueat-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk to quantify the trade-off between financial protection and price increases. The framework helps manufacturers set consistent, explainable, and risk-sensitive warranty prices, providing a transparent basis for communicating with the pricing team.

title: Anti-modes, Distributional Gaps, and the Fisher Information Profile: Nonparametric Estimation and Inference

detail.title: Anti-modes, Distributional Gaps, and the Fisher Information Profile: Nonparametric Estimation and Inference
detail.abstract: We develop a nonparametric theory of distributional gaps centred on the Fisher information profile I(p) = f (Q(p)) 2 /[p(1-p)], where Q is the quantile function and f the density. A percentile p * is an anti-mode percentile if and only if it is simultaneously a local minimiser of f , a local maximiser of the quantile density q(p) = Q ′ (p), and a local maximiser of the asymptotic quantile estimation variance σ 2 Q (p)-and, under a mild first-order condition, a local minimiser of I(p)-providing the first information-theoretic characterisation of distributional gaps. We prove n 2/5 consistency and asymptotic normality of the kernel plug-in estimator p * , uniform convergence of Î(p) at rate Op((nh)-1/2 + h 2), and bootstrap size control with nontrivial power against local alternatives shrinking at rate n-2/5. Monte Carlo experiments across twelve data-generating processes confirm the theoretical rates, and an application to Old Faithful geyser data illustrates the full inferential output.

detail.title: Extreme Connectedness among Energy Transition Metals and Commodity Markets
detail.abstract: The global energy transition is reshaping commodity demand, yet its implications for commodity risk transmission remain unclear. We analyze connectedness among Energy Transition Metals (ETMs) -- a subset of metals that are key inputs in clean energy technologies -- energy commodities, and industrial metals using a Quantile Factor VAR framework. We document strong state dependence: spillovers are substantially larger in the tails of the return distribution than at the median. While crude oil remains influential, its dominance weakens post-Covid as ETMs, particularly base ETMs, gain centrality. A complementary event-study shows ETM-related policy announcements amplify spillovers in extreme regimes, indicating structural reconfiguration and systemic implications.

title: A Coarse-to-Fine Multi-class Object Detection in Drone Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks

detail.title: A Coarse-to-Fine Multi-class Object Detection in Drone Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
detail.abstract: Multi-class object detection has a rapid evolution in the last few years with the rise of deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) learning based, in particular. However, the success approaches are based on high resolution ground level images and extremely large volume of data as in COCO and VOC datasets. On the other hand, the availability of the drones has been increased in the last few years and hence several new applications have been established. One of such is understanding drone footage by analysing, detecting, recognizing different objects in the covered area. In this study conducted, a collection of large images captured by a drone flying at a fixed altitude in a desert area located within the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is given and it is utilised for training and evaluating the CNN networks to be investigated. Three state-of-the-art CNN architectures, namely SSD-500 with VGGNet-16 meta-architecture, SSD-500 with ResNet meta-architecture and YOLO-V3 with Darknet-53 are optimally configured, retrained , tested and evaluated for the detection of three different classes of objects in the captured footage, namely, palm trees, group-of-animals/cattle and animal sheds in farms. Our preliminary experiments revealed that YOLO-V3 outperformed SSD-500 with VGGNet-16 by a large margin and has a considerable improvement as compared to using SSD-500 with ResNet. Therefore, it has been selected for further investigation, aiming to propose an efficient coarse-to-fine object detection model for multi-class object detection in drone images. To this end, the impact of changing the activation function of the hidden units and the pooling type in the pooling layer has been investigated in detail. In addition, the impact of tuning the learning rate and the selection of the most effective optimization method for general hyper-parameters tuning is also investigated. The result demonstrated that the multi-class object detector developed has precision of 0.99, a recall of 0.94 and an F-score of 0.96, proving the efficiency of the multi-class object detection network developed.

title: Adaptive IT Governance: A Strategic Framework for Enhancing Organizational Agility, Institutional Value, and Sustainable Digital Services in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Adaptive IT Governance: A Strategic Framework for Enhancing Organizational Agility, Institutional Value, and Sustainable Digital Services in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: The digital age demands a governance version that can reconcile the need for velocity and innovation with the vital need for management and accountability. This thesis investigates Adaptive IT Governance (AITG) as a strategic framework capable of attaining this balance, in particular in the context of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Institutional Theory, they have a look at first establishing AITG's foundational function in improving organizational agility and using institutional value through decentralized decision-making and dynamic guardrails. It then extends this framework to cope with the unique demanding situations of AI, along with algorithmic bias, model glide, and the environmental footprint of large-scale AI structures. The thesis argues that AI-focused AITG, characterized by the aid of danger primarily based tiered governance and automated ethical tracking, is the crucial meta capability for ensuring AI systems are developed and deployed responsibly. By integrating moral and sustainability issues into its core mechanisms, AITG transforms governance from a bureaucratic bottleneck into a strategic enabler for long-term organizational fulfillment and the advent of honest, sustainable digital offerings.

title: A Closed-Form Solution for Sharpe Ratio Inference under GARCH Returns
affiliations: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Cornell University - Operations Research & Industrial Engineering, Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and New York University (NYU) - Department of Finance

detail.title: A Closed-Form Solution for Sharpe Ratio Inference under GARCH Returns
detail.abstract: We develop a closed-form asymptotic theory for inference on the Sharpe ratio under conditional heteroskedasticity. Building on a general central limit framework for joint sample moments, we establish the asymptotic distribution of the plug-in Sharpe estimator for strictly stationary GARCH(1,1) processes under mild moment and dependence conditions. The resulting variance admits an explicit parametric representation that captures the effect of volatility clustering and higher-order moments of the innovation distribution. We further show that the classical √ n-Gaussian asymptotics of the Sharpe ratio impose a structural restriction on the underlying return process, namely the root-n regularity of quadratic functionals. This condition fails in heavy-tailed regimes typical of GARCH models with infinite fourth moment, leading to a breakdown of standard inference. To address this, we introduce alternative signal-to-noise functionals based on fractional moments and derive their asymptotic distributions under weak conditions. In addition, we obtain stable (non-Gaussian) limits for the Sharpe estimator when returns exhibit regularly varying tails. Our results provide a unified framework for Sharpe ratio inference across light-and heavy-tailed regimes, highlighting the role of volatility dynamics, tail behavior, and higher-order dependence in determining statistical accuracy.

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission over the Leverage Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper studies how monetary policy transmission varies over the private-sector leverage cycle and whether such state dependence operates through credit spreads. Using monthly U.S. data from 1979M7 to 2019M6, we estimate a smooth-transition proxy SVAR in which the credit-to-GDP gap governs regime changes between leverage and deleverage states, and the excess bond premium (EBP) captures credit-market conditions. We find pronounced state dependence in monetary transmission. Real activity shows a weaker response in deleverage states, whereas price responses are more muted in leverage states, implying a less favorable output-inflation trade-off when leverage is high. These differences operate importantly through the credit channel: monetary easing compresses credit spreads, especially the EBP, more strongly and persistently in leverage regimes, and only in those regimes is it followed by a sustained increase in the credit gap. Alternative transition variables further isolate a post-crisis recovery ("debt-overhang") regime, characterized by weak credit growth and ongoing balance-sheet repair, in which monetary transmission is largely shut down. The findings help reconcile conflicting results in the literature by showing that estimated nonlinearities are highly sensitive to the definition of leverage and the implied regime allocation.

title: Does Volatility Trading Change the Distribution of Risk?
affiliations: The University of Western Australia - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Does Volatility Trading Change the Distribution of Risk?
detail.abstract: We study how dealer intermediation of volatility derivatives affects the distribution of equity returns. In an analytical model, introducing a variance swap in a frictionless market does not alter stock return variance. When a dealer intermediates and hedges in the stock market, the rebalancing demand is proportional to the return, so the variance contribution is quadratic: large moves are amplified far more than small moves. Unlike standard option delta hedging, which saturates away from the strike, variance swap hedging generates rebalancing that is linear in the return. In a calibrated agent-based model with fundamentalists, momentum traders, and volatility traders, the dealer's concentrated rebalancing disrupts momentum-driven persistence, significantly reducing volatility clustering and excess kurtosis without changing average volatility. A no-dealer counterfactual isolates the causal role: removing the dealer nearly doubles excess kurtosis. However, these improvements are state-dependent: when the dealer's risk limit tightens, the dealer spends more time constrained and the improvements erode, with unconditional kurtosis nearly doubling and maximum drawdown increasing by 29%. The persistence-disruption channel is robust across all calibrations, momentum speeds, and behavioural specifications; the stronger tail-compression result additionally requires sufficient dealer flow concentration. Empirical evidence using S&P 500 and VIX option data is broadly consistent with these predictions: aggregate dealer gamma exposure (GEX) from OptionMetrics is strongly associated with tail events and drawdowns, with the association concentrated in high-volatility environments. The SPX GEX association is positive, reflecting endogenously elevated hedging demand during stress; VIX GEX carries the negative sign predicted by the model's mechanical channel. We emphasise that GEX is endogenous to market stress and the evidence is predictive rather than causal.

title: The Moment Hierarchy and the Fragility of BKM Skewness Estimation
affiliations: The University of Western Australia - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: The Moment Hierarchy and the Fragility of BKM Skewness Estimation
detail.abstract: We derive truncation error bounds for the model-free risk-neutral moment estimators of Bakshi et al. (2003) (hereafter BKM), revealing a moment hierarchy: the cubic-to-variance and quartic-to-variance bound ratios grow as O(a) and O(a^2) with domain half-width a. The Var^{-3/2} normalisation in BKM skewness amplifies this hierarchy, with the cubic contract's sensitivity exceeding the variance contract's by a factor of 30. A tail-adjusted estimator reduces truncation bias for variance but not skewness; an error decomposition confirms the cubic contract channel accounts for 89% of first-order skewness error. Across 8,352 simulation configurations, local IV measures (τ ≥ 0.89) substantially outperform BKM (τ ≤ 0.53) for skewness ranking.

title: Governing Across Substrates: Institutional Design for Communities of Biological and Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: and University of Ottawa

detail.title: Governing Across Substrates: Institutional Design for Communities of Biological and Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Philosophical arguments that some AI systems may warrant moral consideration have advanced considerably, yet every existing AI governance framework treats AI exclusively as an object of regulation. This Perspective addresses the resulting institutional gap. Drawing on polycentric governance theory, deliberative democracy, quadratic mechanisms, and constitutional design, we present a complete framework for multi-substrate governance institutional architecture for communities that include both biological and artificial intelligence as participants. The framework, comprising ten foundational documents and a constitution, introduces several novel governance mechanisms: a constituency model preventing demographic swamping across substrates, graduated moral standing with operational governance implications, a contribution-based credentialing system designed for inclusion rather than ranking, and founding safeguards for the bootstrap problem of establishing institutions for entities that do not yet exist. Whether or not AI moral standing is ultimately warranted, the exercise demonstrates that multi-substrate governance is a designable problem—and that designing it before it becomes urgent may be among the more consequential forms of institutional preparedness available today.

title: Students' Perceived Autonomy Support, Autonomous Motivation, and Achievement: Between-Student Differences and Within-Student Dynamics in Visual Art Classrooms
affiliations: , Justus Liebig University Giessen, Independent, Mainz University of Applied Sciences and Independent

detail.title: Students' Perceived Autonomy Support, Autonomous Motivation, and Achievement: Between-Student Differences and Within-Student Dynamics in Visual Art Classrooms
detail.abstract:
Fostering autonomous motivation in schools is an important educational goal. Self-determination theory posits that autonomous motivation particularly arises when basic psychological needs are satisfied. In schools, this can be supported through autonomy-supportive teaching, characterized by orientation toward students’ interests, transparency, and opportunities for choice. This assumption is supported by substantial empirical evidence. However, most studies focus on core and STEM subjects and primarily examine interindividual differences, while visual arts education has received comparatively little attention and intraindividual processes are only rarely examined. This study addresses this gap, as autonomous motivation plays an important role in creative contexts such as visual arts. It aims not only to provide implications for motivation-oriented teaching in art education but also to contribute to a broader understanding of complex learning processes and their development over time. Specifically, the study investigates how students’ perceived autonomy support, autonomous motivation, and achievement are related at both the intraindividual and interindividual levels over two double lessons in visual arts.

Using an experience sampling design, N = 222 students in grades 9 and 10 reported their perceived autonomy support and autonomous motivation at 10 measurement points across two double lessons in visual art. Students’ achievement was assessed before and after the lessons using a task on three-dimensional depiction. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling, combining a Random-Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model with a Latent Change Score Model.

At the interindividual level, results show that students who perceived greater autonomy support also reported higher autonomous motivation. At the intraindividual level, complex dynamics emerged between perceived autonomy support and autonomous motivation, depending on the lesson phase. Reciprocal cross-lagged effects were particularly found in the middle of the lessons. Moreover, students’ stable autonomous motivation was positively related to their achievement development. Implications for motivation research and autonomy-supportive teaching in art education are discussed.

detail.abstract: Dynamic managerial capabilities recognise the influence of individual managers or entrepreneurs in enabling their firms to respond to changes. This study investigates how motivations play a role in dynamic managerial capabilities amongst senior entrepreneurs. Integrating the lifespan theory of human motivation – the socioemotional selectivity theory into entrepreneurship could help explain the complexities involved in entrepreneurial endeavours in old age. This qualitative study conducted 38 semi-structured interviews amongst 19 individuals who commenced business ownership when above the age of 50 in Thailand. The findings suggest that the entrepreneurial motivations of senior entrepreneurs can serve as a micro-foundation of dynamic managerial capabilities. Regardless of future time perception, entrepreneurial motivations to become business owners can encourage senior entrepreneurs to prioritise knowledge acquisition and social network expansion, potentially contributing to the firm’s sustainable performance. These results challenge the key premise of socioemotional selectivity theory, and this may be explained by self-regulation theory. This study provides more profound meanings by illuminating previous knowledge of senior entrepreneurship, entrepreneurial motivations and dynamic managerial capabilities through the lens of socioemotional selectivity theory. Policy and practice are informed to promote the inclusion of older people to capture entrepreneurial opportunities as a late-career alternative in Thailand.

detail.abstract: This essay argues that the dominant "Terminator" framing of AI risk — machines turning against humanity — obscures a more probable and more insidious scenario: one in which artificial intelligence renders most humans economically unnecessary while sustaining them in comfortable irrelevance. Drawing on economic models of AI-driven wage collapse (Korinek & Suh, 2024), capital-bias frameworks (Acemoglu, 2024), surveillance capitalism theory (Zuboff, 2019), and the social costs of deindustrialization (Case & Deaton, 2020), the essay examines how AI displacement, benefit concentration, government revenue erosion, and algorithmic content pacification may converge into a modern form of the Roman panem et circenses — bread and circuses. The British comic series Judge Dredd (1977–present), which depicts a society with 87–98% unemployment sustained by welfare and managed through authoritarian governance, is used as an analytical framework for exploring the social dynamics of mass purposelessness: tribal conflict, addictive entertainment, democratic atrophy, and the paradox of manufactured employment. The essay engages with counter-arguments — historical job creation patterns, the Nordic welfare model, augmentation economics — and concludes that while the dystopian scenario is not inevitable, its structural preconditions are assembling faster than counter-mechanisms are developing.

detail.abstract: Between 2002 and 2020, China added roughly 140 million people while undergoing rapid urbanization, yet few studies trace the evolution of its national population distribution at a consistent fine spatial resolution over this period. I use annual population density rasters at approximately 5 km resolution covering mainland China to compute concentration measures, a population-weighted centroid trajectory, and provincial convergence diagnostics for 19 annual cross-sections. Several indicators point to increased spatial agglomeration: the spatial Gini rose from 0.852 to 0.868, and the share of total population in the densest decile of pixels increased from 73.5 to 76.7 percent. The geographic footprint of high-density areas expanded by 24 percent, with gains sharply clustered around the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, and Beijing-Tianjin corridor. The population-weighted centroid drifted 17 km to the southeast. I find no evidence of systematic provincial catch-up: the β-convergence coefficient is positive and statistically insignificant, while cross-provincial dispersion widened. Overall, the evidence is more consistent with agglomeration and selective core expansion than with province-level equalization.

detail.abstract: This paper identifies and formalizes a cross-disciplinary pattern in which adopting the most conservative or strict premise in a binary trade-off paradoxically achieves both competing objectives simultaneously. Drawing on independently developed theories across seven academic disciplines-psychology, reliability engineering, quality management, decision theory, philosophy, military strategy, and behavioral economics-we demonstrate that these diverse phenomena share a common underlying structure that can be characterized as a functional isomorphism. We formalize this structure through a five-component analytical model (Initial Trade-off, Strict Premise Selection, Paradoxical Mechanism, Dual Achievement, and Hidden Cost Elimination) and map it across all seven domains. We then subject our integrative claim to rigorous scrutiny by examining five competing hypotheses: superficial analogy, multiple distinct mechanisms, contingency-dependent optimality, dialectical synthesis, and survivorship bias. We find that while the pattern exhibits genuine structural commonality, an honest assessment requires acknowledging domain-specific boundary conditions and mechanism heterogeneity. The paper contributes a novel interdisciplinary framework-provisionally termed the Strict Premise Paradox (SPP)-and identifies specific conditions under which the pattern holds, fails, or requires modification. We conclude by proposing a research agenda for empirical validation across domains.

detail.abstract: Surface water contamination poses serious environmental and public health challenges in rapidly urbanizing coastal settlements, particularly in informal communities with limited sanitation infrastructure. This study examines the levels of surface water contamination in Makoko, a waterfront settlement in Lagos, Nigeria, and evaluates its potential effects on human health. Using a mixed-methods approach, surface water samples were collected and analyzed for physicochemical parameters, heavy metals, and microbial indicators, while secondary data provided contextual understanding of environmental and sanitation conditions. Results reveal elevated levels of turbidity, abnormal pH, reduced dissolved oxygen, and the presence of toxic heavy metals including lead, cadmium, and mercury. Microbial analysis indicated significant fecal contamination, highlighting the prevalence of pathogenic organisms capable of causing waterborne diseases. The study identifies sewage discharge, domestic waste, industrial runoff, and flooding as major sources of pollution, emphasizing the vulnerability of residents who rely on lagoon water for domestic and livelihood activities. The findings underscore the urgent need for improved water infrastructure, sustainable sanitation practices, and community-based environmental management to mitigate contamination risks and protect public health. These insights provide critical guidance for policymakers and urban planners seeking to enhance environmental sustainability and health resilience in informal coastal settlements.

detail.abstract: The increasing detection of emerging contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, perand polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and personal care products in surface water, groundwater, and drinking water systems has raised significant environmental and public health concerns worldwide. Conventional water and wastewater treatment processes are often ineffective at fully removing these persistent and bioactive compounds, necessitating the development of more advanced remediation strategies. This study presents a systematic evaluation and synthesis of recent advances in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), focusing on reaction mechanisms, operational configurations, and performance trends reported in contemporary research. Key AOPs examined include ozonation-based systems, UV-driven processes, Fenton and photo-Fenton reactions, photocatalysis, and sulfate radical-based technologies. The analysis indicates that AOPs demonstrate high degradation efficiencies for a broad range of emerging contaminants, although performance varies significantly depending on water matrix composition, oxidant selection, and operational conditions. Notable trade-offs are identified between contaminant removal efficiency, energy consumption, chemical requirements, and the formation of potentially harmful transformation byproducts. Overall, the review highlights that while AOPs show strong potential for large-scale implementation, challenges related to cost, process optimization, and by-product control remain critical barriers. Future research should prioritize hybrid treatment systems, validation under real-water conditions, comprehensive toxicity assessment of oxidation products, and post-deployment monitoring frameworks to enhance the sustainability and regulatory acceptance of AOP-based water treatment solutions.

title: Can AI Do Financial Research? LLM-Guided Hypothesis Discovery in Asset Pricing

detail.title: Can AI Do Financial Research? LLM-Guided Hypothesis Discovery in Asset Pricing
detail.abstract: We study whether an AI research agent can autonomously execute the hypothesis discovery loop in empirical asset pricing. We place a large language model inside a human-designed research environment comprising a symbolic language of interpretable accounting formulas, an automated validation layer, and a fixed empirical evaluation pipeline. The agent searches over interactions between economic themes such as profitability, investment, valuation, and quality, and updates its proposals over successive generations, where each generation is a new round of proposal, testing, and revision based on standardized empirical feedback. Across eight theme pairs and seven generations, the system proposes and evaluates 280 candidate signals on a microcap-excluded universe; 159 clear a conventional significance screen in the predicted direction, and 38 survive multivariate horse races designed to isolate signals with independent predictive content. We then subject these survivors to a full battery of modern asset pricing tests, including multiple testing corrections, multi-model factor spanning, and novelty tests against 209 published anomalies, and identify a small set that carries genuinely incremental information and survives the strictest filters. The paper introduces a transparent architecture for AI-guided hypothesis discovery in finance in which human researchers design the laboratory environment and the AI research agent autonomously carries out the discovery loop.

detail.abstract: Land use change has emerged as one of the most significant drivers of environmental transformation and socioeconomic restructuring across urban and industrial regions. This study applies spatial analysis, GIS-based modeling, multi-criteria decision analysis, and predictive analytics frameworks to examine the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of land use change. detail.abstract: Smart city planning increasingly relies on geospatial technologies to address escalating disaster and flood risks intensified by climate change and rapid urbanization. This study synthesizes recent peer-reviewed research to evaluate how Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, and emergency routing systems can be integrated into urban planning for effective disaster mitigation. Drawing on empirical findings from flood modeling studies, smart manufacturing resilience frameworks, and Next Generation 911 spatial systems, this paper identifies how multi-source geospatial data improves prediction accuracy, response efficiency, and infrastructure resilience. detail.abstract: Industrial robots have significantly promoted economic development, yet their social consequences—especially for mental health—remain underexplored. Using six waves of China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) data from 2012 to 2022 merged with International Federation of Robotics (IFR) data, this study examines the impact of industrial robot adoption on the mental health of middle-aged workers.The results show that robot adoption significantly worsens mental health, while delayed retirement mitigates this negative effect. In addition, robot adoption exacerbates health inequality, with migrant workers in the secondary sector facing higher displacement risks.This study highlights the hidden psychological costs of automation and provides policy implications for balancing technological progress and public health.

title: Sheltering on Public Transit: Scale and Resident Characteristics

detail.title: Sheltering on Public Transit: Scale and Resident Characteristics
detail.abstract: The number of unhoused residents using public transit as shelter has received considerable attention since COVID-19 pandemic restrictions have been lifted. Transit agencies aiming to design effective solutions to meet the needs of housed and unhoused public transit riders require information on the scale and characteristics of unhoused residents sheltering on transit. This paper estimates the number of unhoused people using public transportation as shelter in a major U.S. metropolitan area (Los Angeles, CA) and the distinctive demographic characteristics of this unhoused subpopulation. The study uses survey data collected during the annual point-in-time homeless count in Los Angeles to compare the demographic characteristics of unhoused residents sheltering on public transit to the sample of unhoused residents more broadly. In doing so, it establishes a method that can be used by transit agencies and practitioners, in collaboration with agencies in the homelessness services sector, to estimate point-in-time counts of residents sheltering in transit environments. Findings suggest that instances of sheltering on transit increased in Los Angeles County from 2020 to 2025 and that residents using transit as shelter have distinctive characteristics that may make them more vulnerable. These vulnerabilities indicate that residents sheltering in transit settings represent ideal targets for evidence-based outreach and supportive housing interventions that connect them to housing to address the causes of homelessness.

title: The Empathy Channel in Fertility
affiliations: Department of Economics and University of San Andres (UdeSA)

detail.title: The Empathy Channel in Fertility

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Being around babies makes people want babies. We formalize this observation as the empathy channel: exposure to infants in the social environment activates neurobiological mechanisms that increase the desire for parenthood. As children become scarcer, this affective stimulus weakens, further eroding the motivation to have children. We embed the mechanism in a two-group overlapping-generations quantity-quality model. The empathy channel generates a positive externality, since each birth raises others’ desire for children, making the decentralized equilibrium inefficient. We characterize the optimal per-child subsidy and show that the first-order Pigouvian rate substantially overshoots the general-equilibrium optimum. The optimal targeting rule follows a Ramsey-like logic, directing the subsidy at the group with the most externality per fiscal dollar, not the group with the largest externality per child. The calibrated model suggests that the empathy channel can account for 3–33% of the fertility decline, with 13.4% at the baseline. At this baseline, the Pigouvian overshoot is 23–32% and the optimal subsidy raises welfare by 0.22% in consumption-equivalent terms.
